target_moa.text: Ozanimod is a sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator that binds with high affinity to S1P receptors 1 and 5 and blocks the capacity of lymphocytes to egress from lymph nodes, reducing lymphocytes in peripheral blood.

citations.quote: Ozanimod is a sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator that binds with high affinity to S1P receptors 1 and 5. Ozanimod blocks the capacity of lymphocytes to egress from lymph nodes, reducing the number of lymphocytes in peripheral blood. The mechanism by which ozanimod exerts therapeutic effects in multiple sclerosis is unknown but may involve the reduction of lymphocyte migration into the central nervous system.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=4%): upper respiratory infection (26% vs 23% IFN beta-1a), hepatic transaminase elevation (10% vs 5%), orthostatic hypotension (4% vs 3%), urinary tract infection (4% vs 3%), back pain (4% vs 3%), and hypertension (4% vs 2%). Serious risks include infections, bradycardia/AV conduction delays, and liver injury.
